knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Isolating the area and protecting yourself comes before any cleaning step.
Recapping and bending cause sharps injuries. Handling by the barrel and using a container is the approach.
The label and the organisational procedure set the dilution and contact time, not memory or appearance.

practicalCriteria: In a scenario with a simulated spill, the learner isolates the area and puts on the full PPE set in the correct order, observed by the assessor
The learner disinfects the simulated spill using a supplied product label, and the assessor checks the contact time is met
The learner handles a simulated used sharp into a container without recapping, and completes the exposure steps for a simulated contact
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of the spill scenario
Contact-time check against the supplied label
stopWorkCriteria: Stop immediately if the spill is beyond training or the person is hurt; escalate
Stop any step that involves recapping a needle
Stop any cleaning where the product label or procedure is not available
